title: Business rules live in the database, not the UI
problem: In the no-code prototype, the free-plan patient limit and the subscription tier were enforced only in the browser, so they could be bypassed.
decision: Move the free-plan limit into a Postgres trigger with locking, so concurrent requests can't bypass it. Every table has Row Level Security with per-dietitian isolation. SECURITY DEFINER functions run with a fixed search_path, privileges revoked and then granted explicitly.
verified: 238 RLS integration tests run in CI against Supabase in Docker.

title: A payment can't be cancelled by a race
problem: Two simultaneous payment-gateway events could cancel the subscription of a customer who had paid.
decision: The Asaas webhook is idempotent, validates signatures on the raw body, and uses optimistic concurrency.
verified: A real bug caught in review, then fixed.

title: The AI assistant never sees patient names
problem: Anna, the in-product assistant, answers clinical-practice questions over health data that is sensitive under LGPD art. 11.
decision: Patients are pseudonymized (P1, P2…), and national ID, phone and email are masked. Clinical scope limits are enforced. A monthly AI quota is reserved in the database and refunded if the call fails.
verified: A live evaluation suite (eval:anna) tests the assistant's behavior.

title: Near-zero fixed cost
problem: An early-stage product needs hosting it can afford before revenue, under terms that allow commercial use.
decision: Serve the frontend from Cloudflare Workers (Static Assets). Vercel Hobby was evaluated and rejected because its terms prohibit commercial use.
verified: Deployed to staging and production through the same reusable pipeline.

title: Migration that respects deletion
problem: Data had to move from the no-code prototype without bringing back patients deleted on an LGPD request.
decision: A repeatable migration tool that runs as a dry run by default and never resurrects deleted patients. Deletion removes Storage files first, then the records.
verified: Review caught imports resurrecting deleted patients, and it was fixed.
